rationale: Residual errors show recur_frac>=0.9 and dup_dense_last_frame non-null firing on room_swap and reverse clips, so those signals are downgraded from 'means loop/timewarp' to 'repetition exists' and the guide now selects among loop/reverse/room_swap via echo, seam position, and the judge. Echo is constrained to the ~1e3 moving-content range because the three room_swap wins carry 1e11-1e12 scores from static duplicates, while the true reverse scores 1065. The 'ONE seam => splice' rule is softened to 'splice if same scene, room_swap if the judge reports a different location', which fixes the two room_swap->splice cases without removing splice typing, and the candidate note tells the model to spend a check at the top photo_jump/scene-cut seam for the quiet splice misses.

pack.task: Decide whether this 30s video clip contains an artificial edit, which edit type fits, and which candidates (if any) need a VLM continuity check.
pack.conclude_crit: stop gathering evidence and report the final verdict
pack.judge_crit_template: run the VLM continuity check on candidate {i} at frame {frame} (~{secs:.1f}s)

signals.recur_frac_max: fraction of frames that are near-exact replays of an earlier frame (lag 2-10s). High (>=0.9) means repetition EXISTS, not which edit: a reversed segment duplicates its own footage, and a swapped-in / near-static scene also repeats frames, so >=0.9 supports loop, reverse, room_swap or a static timewarp equally. Use the other signals to choose. Values 0.5-0.8 are ambiguous (same-scene splices reach ~0.6).
signals.dup_dense_last_frame: last frame of a dense run of adjacent-duplicate frames. Consistent with a setpts slowdown, but also fires on any near-static or swapped-in static stretch, so non-null alone is NOT proof of timewarp (it co-occurs with room_swap in the residual errors). Treat non-null as 'timewarp possible', and if a contiguous static repeat region is also present, prefer the static/room_swap reading.
signals.echo_best_score: self-anchored 4-factor score for a reversed segment. Genuine reversals put TWO seams seconds apart that echo each other and score in the ~1e3 range on moving content. Two false-positive families: noise (<10) and astronomically large values (>=1e6), where the matched frames are near-static duplicates — those are artefacts, NOT reversal evidence. A high score marks a reversed SEGMENT, not the whole clip.
signals.scenecut_iframe_frames: frames where the video encoder inserted a scene-cut I-frame; flags abrupt visual discontinuity. BASE RATE: clean clips average ~2-3 of these per 30s from natural motion, so a few are normal. Several widely-spaced entries often mark a scene/location CHANGE (room_swap) rather than a replay.
signals.photo_jump_top3: top frame-difference peaks. z is normalized WITHIN this clip, so the largest peak always scores high even on clean clips — read peak POSITIONS, not z. A top peak coinciding with a scene-cut I-frame marks the most likely seam; do not infer edit TYPE from z.

pack.typing_guide: Typing. recur_frac>=0.9 only means repetition exists (loop, reversed segment, or swapped-in static scene all reach ~1.0) — do NOT type loop on it alone. Then: echo ~1e3 with two seams seconds apart (not the >=1e6 static artefact) => reverse. dup_dense_last_frame non-null => timewarp, unless the dense run is a contiguous static/duplicate stretch. A scene/location change at the seam (top photo_jump peak on a scene-cut I-frame, or judge reporting a different place) => room_swap. A cut inside the SAME scene => splice. ONE confirmed seam is a splice OR a one-sided room_swap, and only the judge separates same-scene from different-scene. No confirmed seam and quiet signals => none.
pack.candidate_note: Each candidate is a transition the gates flagged. BASE RATE: the gates are permissive and nominate ~4-8 candidates per clip INCLUDING on clean clips, so a candidate existing is weak evidence — only its VLM verdict is strong. A check costs ~2s and is near-perfect precision on the break itself. Prioritize candidates whose frame lands on a scenecut_iframe frame or a photo_jump top-3 peak. Splice leaves NO repeat/echo trace, so quiet signals do not rule it out. Crucially, repeat-based verdicts (loop / reverse / timewarp) vs room_swap hinge on whether the seam changes location — a judge-decidable question — so spend a check at the seam before committing.

questions.action: What is the best next step?
questions.corrupted: This clip contains an artificial temporal discontinuity (an edit: replayed footage, reversed segment, swapped scene, cut/splice, or retimed segment).
questions.break_type: Which edit type best fits the evidence?
questions.sufficient: The current evidence is sufficient to conclude with confidence; more VLM checks would not change the verdict.
questions.is_type_template: The evidence indicates this clip was edited with a {type} corruption ({desc}).

type_desc.loop: footage repeats itself — the SAME moving scene is replayed at a seam
type_desc.reverse: a segment plays backward in time
type_desc.room_swap: the scene/location changes to a different place (often then back)
type_desc.splice: a hard cut joins non-contiguous footage of the SAME scene
type_desc.timewarp: part of the clip plays at altered speed (slowed or sped up)
